senses.gloss: An elevator — the British word for it.
examples: Take the *lift* to the fourth floor and turn left.
In London the sign says *lift*, not elevator.
Both *lifts* were out of order, so we walked up.

senses.gloss: A feeling of being cheered up or encouraged.
examples: Her phone call gave me a real *lift*.
The good news was a *lift* for the whole office.
A walk outside usually gives him a *lift*.

senses.gloss: Something that a person enjoys or prefers.
examples: She knows all my *likes* and dislikes.
The form asks about your *likes* in music and food.
Their *likes* and dislikes are almost identical.

senses.gloss: A pale purple color.
examples: The bedroom walls are a soft *lilac*.
She wore *lilac* to the wedding.
The sky turned *lilac* just after sunset.

senses.gloss: A large branch of a tree.
examples: A *limb* came down on the power line during the storm.
The kids nailed boards to the lowest *limb*.
Ice snapped the *limbs* off the old oak.

senses.gloss: A party game in which dancers bend backward to pass under a low bar.
examples: The kids played *limbo* at the birthday party.
He won the *limbo* by bending almost flat.
Somebody put on music and started a game of *limbo*.

senses.gloss: A white powder made from limestone, spread on soil or mixed into mortar.
examples: The farmer spread *lime* to cut the acid in the soil.
Mix the *lime* with sand and water to make mortar.
A bag of garden *lime* costs about six dollars.

senses.gloss: The line where an area ends; its boundary.
examples: The speed drops to 25 inside the city *limits*.
Their farm sits just outside the town *limits*.
Fireworks are banned within the village *limits*.

senses.gloss: A row of people or cars waiting their turn.
examples: There was a *line* out the door at the bakery.
We stood in *line* for forty minutes.
The *lines* at the DMV are shorter on Wednesdays.

senses.gloss: A length of rope, cord, or wire used for a purpose.
examples: Hang the sheets on the *line* to dry.
A fish snapped his *line* right at the boat.
Crews strung new power *lines* along the highway.

senses.gloss: A telephone connection.
examples: The *line* went dead in the middle of the call.
Please hold — I have another *line* ringing.
We had two *lines* installed in the office.

senses.gloss: A row of words in a text, or the words an actor speaks.
examples: Read the third *line* of the poem again.
He forgot his *lines* on opening night.
Her best *line* in the movie is only four words long.

senses.gloss: A large passenger ship that sails a regular route.
examples: The *liner* docked in Miami at dawn.
Her grandparents crossed the Atlantic on an ocean *liner*.
Two cruise *liners* were tied up at the pier.

senses.gloss: A row of people shown to a witness so that a suspect can be picked out.
examples: She picked him out of a police *lineup*.
The suspect stood third from the left in the *lineup*.
No witness could identify anyone in either *lineup*.

senses.gloss: The set of acts, shows, or events scheduled for a program.
examples: The festival announced its *lineup* in March.
The network changed its Thursday night *lineup*.
This year's *lineup* includes three bands from Texas.

senses.gloss: The layer that covers the inside surface of an organ or a container.
examples: Aspirin can irritate the *lining* of the stomach.
The furnace *lining* has to be replaced every few years.
Infection had inflamed the *lining* of his lungs.

senses.gloss: One ring of a chain.
examples: A single *link* snapped and the swing came down.
He shortened the bracelet by two *links*.
Rust had eaten through several *links* of the anchor chain.

senses.gloss: A connection or relationship between two things.
examples: Doctors found a clear *link* between smoking and heart disease.
There is no *link* between the two robberies.
The company still has strong *links* to its founder's family.

senses.gloss: The rim or edge of a container or an opening.
examples: Coffee dripped down the *lip* of the mug.
He stood at the *lip* of the canyon and looked over.
The pitcher has a shaped *lip* for pouring.

senses.gloss: Rude talk back to someone in authority.
examples: Don't give me any *lip*, young man.
The coach won't take *lip* from anyone on the bench.
He got detention for giving a teacher *lip*.

senses.gloss: An entry in a directory or in a published schedule.
senses.ru: запись в справочнике; строка в программе передач
examples: Check the movie *listings* for showtimes.
The phone book *listing* had the wrong address.
Her name appears in the faculty *listing*.

senses.gloss: The way people live from day to day.
examples: The cost of *living* has gone up again.
They moved south for cheaper *living*.
Country *living* suits him better than the city.

senses.gloss: An amount of laundry or other material handled at one time.
examples: I still have two *loads* of laundry to fold.
Wash the towels in a separate *load*.
The truck hauled three *loads* of gravel before noon.

senses.gloss: A large amount or number of something.
examples: There were *loads* of people at the game.
We have a *load* of work to get through today.
She brought back *loads* of photos from the trip.

senses.gloss: A lazy person who avoids work.
examples: He called his brother-in-law a *loafer*.
A few *loafers* were hanging around outside the store.
The foreman has no patience for *loafers*.

senses.gloss: The act of lending something, or the state of being lent.
examples: The painting is on *loan* from a museum in Boston.
Thanks for the *loan* of your truck last weekend.
Several exhibits are here on long-term *loan*.

senses.gloss: A group that tries to influence lawmakers on behalf of an industry or cause.
examples: The gun *lobby* fought the bill in committee.
Farmers have a powerful *lobby* in Washington.
Both *lobbies* spent millions on advertising.

senses.gloss: A piece of hair that hangs together.
examples: A *lock* of hair fell across her forehead.
They kept a *lock* of the baby's hair in an envelope.
Gray *locks* stuck out from under his cap.

senses.gloss: A gated section of a canal that raises or lowers boats.
examples: The barge waited an hour to enter the *lock*.
There are eight *locks* between the two lakes.
Water poured in and lifted the boat inside the *lock*.

senses.gloss: A North American tree with feathery leaves, hard wood, and thorny twigs.
examples: They planted a *locust* by the fence for shade.
Black *locust* makes good fence posts.
The old *locust* in the yard blooms white in May.

senses.gloss: A local branch of a fraternal society, or the hall where it meets.
examples: The *lodge* meets on the first Tuesday of every month.
Her father joined the *lodge* when he was thirty.
Both *lodges* in town raise money for scholarships.

senses.gloss: The dome of sticks and mud that beavers build to live in.
examples: The beavers built a *lodge* at the far end of the pond.
You can see the *lodge* sticking up through the ice.
Beaver *lodges* have their entrances underwater.

senses.gloss: A written record of trips, hours, or events kept in order.
examples: The captain wrote the storm up in the ship's *log*.
Keep a *log* of every mile you drive for work.
Her flight *log* shows two hundred hours.

senses.gloss: An act of looking at something.
examples: Take a *look* at this photo.
One *look* at the sky and we canceled the picnic.
The mechanic had a quick *look* under the hood.

senses.gloss: An expression on someone's face.
examples: She gave me a *look* that ended the conversation.
There was a worried *look* on his face.
I know that *look* — you forgot again, didn't you?

senses.gloss: A person who watches for danger while others work.
examples: One of them stayed outside as a *lookout*.
The *lookout* spotted the boat at first light.
They posted *lookouts* at both ends of the street.

senses.gloss: A silly or crazy person.
examples: The guy on the corner is a harmless *loon*.
You'd have to be a *loon* to swim in that water.
A few *loons* showed up in shorts in January.

senses.gloss: A route or trail that comes back to where it started.
examples: We hiked a five-mile *loop* around the lake.
The shuttle runs a *loop* through downtown.
There are two easy *loops* marked on the trail map.

senses.gloss: A set of instructions that a computer repeats until a condition is met.
examples: The program got stuck in an endless *loop*.
Move that calculation outside the *loop*.
Nested *loops* made the code very slow.

senses.gloss: A defeat in a game or contest.
examples: The team is coming off three straight *losses*.
It was their first *loss* at home all season.
A *loss* on Sunday would end their playoff hopes.

senses.gloss: The death of someone close to you.
examples: I'm so sorry for your *loss*.
The family is still grieving the *loss* of their son.
The whole town felt his *loss*.

senses.gloss: The fact of no longer having something you used to have.
examples: Hearing *loss* runs in his family.
The drug can cause memory *loss*.
*Loss* of sleep was making her irritable.

senses.gloss: A large number or amount of something.
examples: A *lot* of people showed up early.
That's a *lot* to ask of a ten-year-old.
We learned *lots* about the neighborhood that summer.

senses.gloss: An item or group of items sold together at an auction.
examples: *Lot* 42 is a set of silver spoons.
The first three *lots* sold in under a minute.
She bid on a *lot* of old postcards.

senses.gloss: A person's situation or fate in life.
examples: He accepted his *lot* without complaining.
Education improved the *lot* of the whole family.
It is the *lot* of every parent to worry.

senses.gloss: A way of choosing at random among more applicants than there are places.
examples: Spots in the charter school are filled by *lottery*.
Her family entered the visa *lottery* three years running.
Permits for the river are handed out in a spring *lottery*.

senses.gloss: A chemical spray carried to blind and disable an attacker.
examples: She keeps a can of *mace* in her purse.
The guard used *mace* to break up the fight.
*Mace* is legal to carry in most states.

senses.gloss: A warm orange-brown spice made from the covering of the nutmeg seed.
examples: The recipe calls for a pinch of *mace*.
*Mace* tastes like a milder, sweeter nutmeg.
She grinds her own *mace* for the pound cake.

senses.gloss: A tightly run organization, especially a political one that controls votes and jobs.
examples: The city was run by a political *machine* for fifty years.
The party *machine* backed her from the start.
Old *machines* handed out city jobs to loyal voters.

senses.gloss: The amount of protein, carbohydrate, and fat in what a person eats.
examples: He tracks his *macros* in an app.
Her trainer set new *macros* for the off-season.
This bowl fits my *macros* almost exactly.

senses.gloss: A woman who runs a brothel.
examples: The *madam* was arrested along with two of her employees.
She ran the house as its *madam* for twenty years.
The novel's *madam* knows every secret in town.

senses.gloss: The art of performing clever tricks that seem impossible.
examples: He does card *magic* at children's parties.
Her uncle taught her close-up *magic*.
The show mixes comedy and *magic*.

senses.gloss: A special charm or quality that makes something wonderful.
examples: There is a certain *magic* about the first snow.
The band lost its *magic* after the singer left.
Live theater has a *magic* that television can't match.

senses.gloss: A person, place, or thing that attracts people strongly.
examples: The new library has become a *magnet* for teenagers after school.
Cheap rent turned the block into a *magnet* for artists.
Warm weather makes the boardwalk a *magnet* on weekends.

senses.gloss: A piece of advertising or campaign literature sent through the mail.
examples: Voters got three *mailers* from the same candidate.
The dealership sends a *mailer* every spring.
That attack *mailer* probably cost him the election.

senses.gloss: An army or air force officer ranking just above a captain.
examples: She was promoted to *major* last year.
The *major* briefed the unit at dawn.
Two *majors* signed the report.

senses.gloss: A student whose main subject is a particular field.
examples: He's a biology *major* at a state school.
The class is required for all history *majors*.
As an art *major*, she spends most nights in the studio.

senses.gloss: The combination of parts or people that form something.
examples: The *makeup* of the jury worried both lawyers.
Soil *makeup* varies from one field to the next.
Genetic *makeup* explains only part of the risk.

senses.gloss: A thick milkshake made with malted milk powder.
examples: He ordered a chocolate *malt* and fries.
The diner still makes *malts* in a metal cup.
A vanilla *malt* costs four dollars here.

senses.gloss: A car whose gears the driver shifts by hand.
examples: She learned to drive on a *manual*.
The rental company had one *manual* left on the lot.
*Manuals* are getting hard to find in the US.
